claims.title: Finite exact-integer grid sampler and contextual coherence removal

quoted_fields.interface: Basis input and complete computational-basis output of an open even square grid. Four disjoint matching layers cycle horizontal-even, horizontal-odd, vertical-even and vertical-odd. At each actual pair independently: D=(3I+4iZZ)/5 with probability 1-r-epsilon, QD with Q=(12I-5iXX)/13 and probability epsilon, or trace both qubits and replace by I/4 with probability r. Categories are state-independent; old reset outcomes, fresh preparation bits and all classical control are retained in the proof. The finite holdout freezes 4096 component entries, 20000 amplitude bits, bridge reduction, terminal measurement, ordering and implementation hashes before fresh seeds. Experimental streams use OS-seeded Python PRNGs; the exact-law theorem assumes ideal unbiased randomness.
quoted_fields.failure: The bridge identity preserves final Z-output plus reset-record law, not local quantum channels or arbitrary intermediate conditional states. Preserve parallel occurrences and all classical feedforward. Diagonal gates can couple different cycle blocks; neither block count nor cycle rank certifies an efficient full sampler. Tiny exact checks do not verify every implementation path. The favorable-rate 99% bound is statistical and assumes the source protocol, fixed algorithm and independent ideal trials; the supplied PRNG experiment is distinct from ideal unbiased randomness. At epsilon=1/20 all twenty 1024-site pilot draws abort, and five-record matched exact/MPS trials abort five/four times. No speed superiority, general noisy-circuit result, polynomial tail theorem, hardware advance or novelty claim.
